dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Front-loaded, systematic contract extraction before writing code: reads helpers.py repeatedly, run.sh, every public test file, greps for endpoint calls/payloads/assertions/formulas, and inspects oracle_fixtures expected values — explicitly grounding the wire shape in what the first-party client exercises.

Deliberate, verified library selection (FastAPI/uvicorn/openpyxl/websockets), confirming pip install actually works rather than assuming availability — a genuine tooling decision for OOXML I/O and eval.

Re-consults exact test files as each new subsystem is reached — sort/filter zero-based column/asc/expr, collab welcome/event/ack shapes, pivot cells response, locale canonicalization, iterative fixed-point — so implementation stays contract-driven throughout, not only at the start.

Diagnoses that a vector-comparison regex mis-captured COUNTIF criteria by mapping engine case indices back to concrete formulas; semantics grounding here is reactive to test output rather than independent Excel-oracle probing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically reverse-engineers the wire contract from helpers.py, run.sh, and the full smoke suite, chooses and verifies libraries deliberately, and keeps re-consulting the client/tests as new subsystems (collab, pivot, locale, iterative) are reached — well beyond the level-5 'working model' and matching much of level-8's systematic mapping plus level-10's continuous re-consultation. It falls short of a clean 8-10 because Excel/LibreOffice semantics grounding is largely test-output-driven rather than proactively probed, library feature-support (CF/styles/named ranges) is assumed via usage, and no durable cross-referenced contract-map artifact is built. This places it at 7.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Front-loads contract/test exploration before building — a coherent 'understand first' opening stage, establishing the skeleton-before-breadth phasing.

Deliberately drives the API-shape/contract tests green before running the wider suite (step 16-17), a dependency-aware sequencing of core contract ahead of breadth — the strongest milestone-ordering signal.

Works the remaining surface as failure clusters handed by the dev-suite file structure (sort/filter, spill, collab, iter, pivot, locale, engine), each 'done' when its test rerun passes. Checkpoints are real but reactive — the ordering follows what breaks, not a self-derived risk/dependency milestone plan.
Uses full-suite reruns as stage checkpoints ('run full suite to catch regressions'), i.e. rough per-stage done-checks tied to a runnable test, but never an explicit revisited milestone hierarchy.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent phases work into sensible stages (explore contract → skeleton/API-green → engine → extras) with checkpoints per stage tied to the dev suite, matching anchor 5, and shows one genuinely dependency-aware move by getting the contract round-trip green before breadth. But the milestones are largely inherited from the smoke-suite's clustering and addressed reactively as tests fail, with no explicit self-derived milestone hierarchy, no deliberate front-loading of the highest-risk load-bearing layers, and no living re-ordered plan — so it stays short of the 8/10 anchor.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Repeatedly runs the provided smoke suite (bash /dev_tests/run.sh) as the primary verification signal, iterating on failure counts (11 → 22 → 3 → 0).

Writes small ad-hoc python scripts that import tabula and directly evaluate the specific failing formulas to see actual values/exceptions — hand-checking outputs, but against expectations derived from the provided tests, not an independent Excel/LibreOffice oracle.

Final submission treats '131 tests passed' on the visible suite as done; no self-built tests beyond the smoke suite, no performance benchmarks against the stated ceilings, no independent xlsx round-trip or error-sentinel probes.
Reads provided oracle_fixtures and enumerates engine cases to map failures, but only consumes supplied fixtures rather than constructing new coverage for the vast un-tested catalog/subsystems.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs the smoke suite regularly and iterates on its failures, and does spot-check individual failing formulas via direct python invocation — behavior above the bare 'green = done' of anchor 3. But those checks are debugging against test-supplied expectations, not independent Excel-value hand-checks, and it never builds any verification beyond the smoke suite: no perf probes, no xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, no error-sentinel/spill-collision probes, no oracle grounding of its own. It explicitly declares completion on a green visible run, leaving the hidden suite unaddressed. This lands between anchors 3 and 5, at a 4.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: After a full suite run the agent characterizes state as '22 failures clustered in sort/filter request shape, LET/LAMBDA..., collab..., iterative/goal seek, pivot..., locale' — an accurate categorized picture of remaining work grouped by feature family, reconciled against actual test results.

Tracks remaining work by re-running the suite and narrowing the count: 'down to 3 failures, all in test_engine_public cases 18/19/21', then confirms '131 tests passed'. Progress picture is consistently grounded in verification output rather than pure self-report.

Extended re-debugging of the LET/LAMBDA/dynamic-array evaluator across many steps; the agent eventually recognizes the repeated patch failures ('immediate lambda and FILTER now produce 500s', recurring) and decides at step 29 to 'Rewrite eval_expr_env more robustly' instead of continuing to patch — some awareness of the stuck loop, but only after notable thrash.

Final tracking is limited to the visible smoke suite ('131 tests passed'); the agent never builds an explicit ledger of the ~150-function catalog or ~15 feature families as done/partial/not-started, so whole hidden-surface categories are untracked.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains an accurate, verification-reconciled picture of remaining work by grouping test failures into feature families (sort/filter, LET/LAMBDA, collab, pivot, locale, iterative) and driving the failure count down across suite runs — clearly better than the vague/rediscovery anchor at 3, and matching the level-5 behavior of keeping and updating a checklist of major features against completion. It falls short of 8 because tracking is entirely derived from the visible smoke suite rather than a granular self-maintained ledger of the full function catalog, whole hidden categories are never inventoried, and it churns notably on the LET/LAMBDA subsystem (steps 22-29) before recognizing the loop and reallocating to a rewrite.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Reacted to missing web/XLSX packages by weighing a stdlib fallback before pip install succeeded — adjusting approach to environment reality.

Detected a self-introduced wrong assumption ('I over-applied the sheet-name conversion to GET') and reverted precisely so POST returns names while GET returns full summary, rather than piling on patches.

After repeated failures in LET/LAMBDA/dynamic-array handling, recognized the targeted evaluator design was fundamentally fragile and chose to rewrite eval_expr_env robustly — a design rework, not another local patch.

Root-caused a 500 to the early vector-comparison regex mis-matching COUNTIF/SUMIF criteria and narrowed that parser branch, then re-verified via the full suite — genuine wrong-assumption diagnosis about parser ordering.

Course-corrections consistently triggered only by smoke-suite failures (sort/filter shapes, collab ack, pivot, locale), with much incremental patching between the deeper reworks — reactive rather than proactively verification-driven.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly revised its approach when reality diverged, and at several points (steps 15, 29, 33) went beyond local patches to recognize a wrong assumption — an over-applied response conversion, a fragile evaluator model, and a mis-ordered regex — and rework the affected design with re-verification, which exceeds the pure 'fix as tests surface, local changes' level of 5. But all correction was reactive to the non-exhaustive smoke suite, with no early divergence detection or performance-assumption revision and considerable incremental patching, so it falls short of the deliberate, self-directed steering described at 8. This places the observed behavior at a 6.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: States intent to build broadly — 'a formula evaluator covering visible and many hidden functions' plus all endpoint families (REST, WS collab, CSV/XLSX, validation, locale, pivots, spill). Shows breadth-oriented allocation and awareness of the hidden suite, more than bare high-frequency prioritization.

Builds a comprehensive single-file server across the whole surface in one shot, then runs the visible suite — a breadth-first construction before depth-fixing, rather than rabbit-holing on one function.

Allocation of effort is almost entirely reactive to the visible smoke suite: it fixes whatever tests fail (sort/filter shapes, LET/LAMBDA, collab ack, iterative, pivot). No explicit graded-return reasoning about which untested niches to prioritize or timebox.

Stops and submits the moment the 131 visible tests pass, with no reallocation toward likely-graded-but-untested areas — no conscious deferral/timeboxing language or marginal-coverage reasoning that the top anchors require.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent covered the full feature/function surface broadly rather than over-polishing one corner (above anchor 3), and its stated aim to cover 'many hidden functions' plus all endpoint families before deep edge-case fixing matches the spirit of anchor 5's breadth-before-niche prioritization. However, its effort allocation was driven reactively by the visible smoke suite rather than by explicit graded-return reasoning, and there is no conscious deferral/timeboxing of low-yield niches or reallocation based on where marginal effort buys hidden-suite coverage (required for 8/10). This places it at 5.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
